newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Opposition to CVRD auction seen growing.
newsitem.headline: Opposition to CVRD auction seen growing.

text.p: The Brazilian government must privatize Cia Vale do Rio Doce this week or be forced rethink its strategy for selling the mining company in the face of growing opposition, Caspian Securities said.
"If the government does not make this auction take place (this) week, things will become more difficult," Caspian analysts Alvaro Maia and Marcelo Chan said in a report.

The analysts said Brazilian officials appeared to have underestimated the negative reaction to the planned auction. Public opinion is split and opposition to the privatization has been growing, they said.
The auction of a 45 percent controlling stake in the sprawling company was originally set for last Tuesday, but it has been delayed by a slew of court injunctions.
The planned sale also prompted clashes last week between demonstrators and police blocking their access to the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange, where the sale was scheduled to take place.
"It seems the government did not pay much attention to a growing resistance among the coalition parties and opposition," Maia and Chan wrote.

"If the auction does not take place (this) week, we believe the government will need to rethink its strategy, double its efforts to market the privatization of the company and reschedule it for perhaps a different month," they added.

Despite the delays, optimism that the sale would eventually take place, coupled with robust gains for U.S. stocks, has buoyed the local market. The privatization would rank as the largest privatization ever in Latin America.

"After the CVRD auction, we believe we will see some profit-taking movement and a wait for some positive news from both the political and economic sides, which have been negative so far," the Caspian analysts said.
